Sofia — thanks for flagging. Proposal below based on current AP/AR practice and VAT rules: 

1) Apply cash against the explicit invoice references in the remit file where amounts match exactly. For INV-2026-1192 and INV-2026-1208 the remit lines map cleanly — apply those.
2) For INV-2027-0021 (reverse charge) we need to book the gross amount to the invoice and set tax flag to "reverse_charge" in our ledger. No VAT reclaim on our side; just tagging for reporting. Marcus — confirm that your ledger mapping for INV-2027-0021 uses tax code RC2027.
3) Apply CM-88 as a partial offset to INV-2026-1192 (customer expects it against that invoice per their note). If there's a residual balance after exact mappings, allocate remainder to oldest outstanding invoice under the same legal entity.
4) Because cash hit the virtual collection account, we'll create a split cash application journal referencing ACHREF 987654321 and post to the three invoice IDs with the VAT flags. Vanessa — please add a VAT note in the transaction memo so downstream reporting shows reverse-charge for INV-2027-0021.

If you want, I can draft the confirmation email to Crescent outlining the applied invoices and remaining balance.

-Laura
